blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – No Filipinos were harmed in the recent protests in France and Italy, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said Monday morning. “Per the latest reports from the Philippine Embassy in Paris and the Philippine Consulate General in Milan, no Filipinos have been reported to be involved or harmed in the protests,” DFA spokesperson Analyn Ratonel said in a text message to reporters. Over the weekend, nationwide protests erupted in France over the rising cost of living. The demonstrations later descended into what French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu described as “violence of extreme intensity.” READ: France counts cost of violent protests, 1,800 arrested Along the streets of Paris, cars were torched and shops were reportedly ransacked, leading to 1,800 arrests and 150 police officers being injured. Likewise, the rising cost of living in Milan led to clashes between protesters and riot police, looting and arson, the Associated Press reported. Although the demonstration started peacefully, 50 individuals were later detained and two police officers were injured. /dl READ: ‘Free the mountains’: Clashes at Milan protest over Winter Olympics...
